newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse may focus now on holding companies.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse may focus now on holding companies.

text.p: The Brussels Stock Exchange may switch its gaze to holding companies in the near term after strong gains by Cobepa on Monday focused attention on market laggards, dealers said.
But some warned that stock pickers hoping to cash in on any potential the holdings have for closing their share price discount to net asset value may be asking for trouble.
The Bel-20 leading share index put on a brave show on Monday, eeking out a 0.03 percent gain to 1,887.74 points in the face of early weakness on Wall Street.
Cobepa, not a Bel-20 component, rose 6.0 percent to 1,230 francs, a new record high.

According to BBL analyst Herman Van Der Loos, who said he put Cobepa on the bank's buy list last week, the move helped narrow Cobepa's discount to net asset value to around 24 percent from over 25 percent. A further small gain was possible.

Van Der Loos said, however, that investors hoping to "catch the train are probably too late." In the long run, he preferred holding company Gevaert, which lost 10 to 2,130 francs on Monday after hitting recent highs.
The countries flagship holdings GBL and Societe Generale de Belgique were on BBL's buy list too, but had given investors poor returns in the past, he noted.

The spark that lit Cobepa's fire was a weekend newspaper interview given by chairman Pierre Scohier in which, among other comments, he saw further changes in the structure of its 17-percent owned GIB retailing group.
French retailer Promodes denied a suggestion from Scohier that it could take a stake in GIB's GB supermarket unit. But GIB, reversed early losses to end up two at 1,422 francs.
Heavyweight Bel-20 component Bekaert bucked the overall firm trend, however, slipping 950 francs, or 3.7 percent to 24,950 francs. One trader said he did not know what was the reason for the fall.
